sources.note: No phonology or prosody. Reports 'they speak Malayalam mixed with Kannada words (Menon 1996:313; Shashi and Shri 1994)', lexical similarity 88% Kalanadi, 83% Kunduvadi, 72% Malayalam, 79% Paniya, 76-80% Mullu Kurumba, 70-74% Wayanad Kurichiya (from the unpublished 2004 SIL/NLCI survey), status 6a, unwritten.

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13(7), July 2013, 58 pp.
sources.note: Does not cover Pathiya at all (sketches Adiya, Aranadan, Bettakurumba, Cholanaickan, Irula, Kakkala, Kani, Kurichiya, Malamuthan, Malaveda, Mannan, Muduga, Mullukurumba). Examined as the most likely open survey of Kerala tribal speech; negative.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2006. Change Request Number 2006-002: create [pty] Pathiya (submitted by Barb Waugh, SIL; adopted 2007-07-18). 7 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Gives lexical-similarity percentages (72% Malayalam, 88% Kalanadi, 83% Kunduvadi, 79% Paniya) from the unpublished NLCI survey (Mathew et al. 2004) and quotes Shashi/Menon 'Malayalam mixed with Kannada words'.

sources.citation: Menon, T. Madhava (ed.). 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Entry 'PATHIYAN' by M. Sasikumar, pp. 313-315 (scanned text of the Anna Centenary Library scan, archive.org item aclcpl00000220a778).
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic entry; the only linguistic remark is 'They speak Malayalam mixed with Kannada words.' (p. 314).

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. 1983. Tribes of Kerala: a proposal for reclassification (Notes). International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics 12(2): 496ff. Thiruvananthapuram: Dravidian Linguistics Association.
sources.note: No phonology; a classificatory note by a Kerala tribal-language linguist (author of the Paniya grammar) that merely lists Pathiyar among Kerala tribes with name variants and location. Useful only as evidence that the Kerala University/ISDL tribal-language programme of the 1970s-80s produced no Pathiya description.

sources.citation: von Fuerer-Haimendorf, Christoph. 1952. Ethnographic notes on some communities of the Wynad. The Eastern Anthropologist 6(1): 18-36.
sources.note: Earliest first-hand notes on the 'Padhiyas near Muthanga'; Glottolog holds a scan but it is not on our disks; almost certainly no phonology.

sources.citation: Aiyappan, A. 1948. Report on the Socio-economic Conditions of the Aboriginal Tribes of the Province of Madras. Madras: Government Press (Pathiyan pp. 47, 97).
sources.note: Primary source behind the Menon 1996 entry; ethnographic, cited for origin/religion, not language. Listed only for completeness of the Pathiya record.

sources.citation: Richards, F. J. 1932. Note on the cultural geography of the Wynad. The Indian Antiquary 61: 170-174 (September), 195-197 (October).
sources.note: No phonology. Cultural-geographic survey of Wynad communities with language affiliations for several tribes (Paniyar 'corrupt Malayalam', Ten Kurumbars/Shola Nayaks Kanarese, Edanadan and Mandadan Chettis Kanarese, Wynadan Chettis Malayalam); for the Pathiyans it gives only origin (Punnad, Mysore), Jain spiritual authority, and that at weddings they 'revert to the fashions of their Kanarese forebears'.

sources.citation: Gopalan Nair, C. 1911. Wynad: Its Peoples and Traditions (Malabar Series). Madras: Higginbotham & Co. Chapter 'Pathiyans', pp. 82-85.
sources.note: No phonology content. Only language remark (p. 83): 'they have adopted Malayalam as their mother-tongue, having given up their ancestral language -- Canarese -- long long ago'; plus a folk etymology of the name from Malayalam 'Pathikalayi Irippin' (p. 85). Earliest printed ethnographic account of the community (predates all Glottolog refs); not in Glottolog under path1235.
